content.value_statement: Agent behavior is hard to measure because valid outputs and workflows can vary. This skill helps teams design rubrics, test sets, judge workflows, and quality gates.
actual_capabilities: Defines multi-dimensional rubrics for accuracy, completeness, citations, source quality, and tool efficiency.
Explains test set design across simple, medium, complex, and very complex tasks.
Shows how to combine LLM-as-judge review with human evaluation.
Includes a Python evaluator example with weighted scoring and summary metrics.
Guides continuous evaluation pipelines for baselines, regressions, and production monitoring.
limitations: It does not provide a hosted evaluation service or dashboard.
The included evaluator uses simplified heuristics and needs production judge integration.
It does not include domain-specific gold data or labeled test sets.
Users must define their own pass thresholds, rubric weights, and review process.

use_cases.title: Create release quality gates
use_cases.description: Define pass criteria that compare agent versions before deployment.

use_cases.title: Measure product assistant quality
use_cases.description: Track answer accuracy, completeness, citations, and source quality over time.

use_cases.title: Build research evaluation sets
use_cases.description: Create task samples that cover simple lookups, comparisons, synthesis, and long workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a starter rubric

prompt_templates.title: Design a balanced test set
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate test planning across complexity levels.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a test set for my agent workflow. Include simple, medium, complex, and very complex cases with expected outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an LLM-as-judge workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced automation with human review support.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an LLM-as-judge evaluation plan for these outputs. Include judging prompts, calibration steps, and human review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a production evaluation program
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of quality gates and monitoring.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my agent evaluation process. Identify metric gaps, regression risks, sampling issues, and improvements for production monitoring.

output_examples.input: Request a rubric for a research assistant agent.
output_examples.output: A weighted rubric covering factual accuracy, completeness, citation accuracy, source quality, and tool efficiency.

output_examples.input: Ask for a test set for a support workflow.
output_examples.output: A set of scenarios grouped by complexity, each with expected outcomes and evaluation notes.

output_examples.input: Ask how to monitor agent quality after launch.
output_examples.output: A continuous evaluation plan with sampling, baseline tracking, regression checks, and human review triggers.

best_practices: Evaluate outcomes and process quality instead of requiring one exact execution path.
Use multiple rubric dimensions so one score does not hide important failures.
Combine automated judging with human review for edge cases and high-impact workflows.
anti_patterns: Testing only easy examples that do not match real user behavior.
Changing prompts or tools without a baseline for comparison.
Using a single pass rate without inspecting dimension-level failures.

faq.question: What type of agents can this skill evaluate?
faq.answer: It fits agents that answer questions, use tools, research topics, update state, or complete multi-step workflows.

faq.question: Does this skill run evaluations automatically?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and example code, but users must connect their own agents, judges, and data sources.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is tool-agnostic and supports workflows for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users.

faq.question: What metrics does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It emphasizes factual accuracy, completeness, citation accuracy, source quality, tool efficiency, and overall weighted scores.

faq.question: Do I need human reviewers?
faq.answer: Human reviewers are recommended for calibration, edge cases, high-risk outputs, and checks that automated judges may miss.

faq.question: How should I start?
faq.answer: Start with a small real test set, define clear rubric dimensions, record a baseline, and expand coverage over time.
